---
title: "Exploratory Data Analysis: Day 1"
---

Explore a dataset with a question in mind. Use what you find to decide what to investigate next.

## During class

1. We will model an investigation using Titanic in a live Jupyter notebook.
2. In your initial group, generate several questions about tornadoes.
3. Choose one question and investigate it using visualization.
4. Move into new groups to explain your findings and ask follow-up questions.

[Open the lecture slides](slides.qmd)

## Notebooks for Positron

Download the complete course folder and open that folder in Positron so the notebooks can find the local data. Setup instructions are in the README.

[Download all notebooks and data together](downloads/EDA_Day1_Notebooks_and_Data.zip)

| Notebook | Purpose | Download | Read online |
|---|---|---|---|
| Titanic live scaffold | Complete the analysis live, with setup and prompts supplied | [`.ipynb`](notebooks/titanic_live_scaffold.ipynb) | [Preview](notebooks/titanic_live_scaffold.html) |
| Titanic completed version | Reference code, results, and interpretations | [`.ipynb`](notebooks/titanic_complete.ipynb) | [Preview](notebooks/titanic_complete.html) |
| Tornado starter | Load and understand the data, then conduct your own EDA | [`.ipynb`](notebooks/tornadoes_starter.ipynb) | [Preview](notebooks/tornadoes_starter.html) |
| Plotting reference | Optional syntax support using Titanic examples | [`.ipynb`](notebooks/plotting_reference.ipynb) | [Preview](notebooks/plotting_reference.html) |

## Datasets

The files are bundled with the project. You do not need a data download during class.

- [Titanic CSV](data/titanic.csv): 891 passenger records in the example subset.
- [Tornado CSV](data/tornadoes.csv): 4,706 NOAA SPC whole-track records, **2015-2018**.
- [Data guide](data_dictionary.qmd): row meanings, units, categories, and missing values.
- [Sources and preparation](sources.qmd).

The old slides used a different tornado table covering 2015-2022. All materials here use the bundled NOAA 2015-2018 snapshot.

## What to bring to the discussion

Keep your plot available before regrouping. Be ready to explain your question, the evidence, what changed in your thinking, and what you would investigate next.
